PullRequest.Title: Apply new-session composer layout from Agents settings
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #338483

This changes `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` from application scope to window scope. Agents settings are stored in the sessions workspace configuration, where application-scoped values are filtered out; window scope allows the Agents value to apply while preserving User settings support.

Adds a regression test that verifies the setting remains window-scoped.

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --grep "New session composer layout"` (7 passing)

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or restore an Agents window and load its workspace-scoped settings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing workspace-configuration loader reads or restores the workspace configuration, parses keys allowed by WORKSPACE_SCOPES, and publishes the in-memory configuration model before consumers can observe the setting. The scope change merely allows this one boolean key through the existing parse.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the workspace configuration through the existing cached or file-service-backed configuration loader.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical workspace configuration load per initialization/reload, independent of the number of settings; this diff adds no extra read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same workspace configuration was loaded and parsed, but APPLICATION-scoped values were excluded from WORKSPACE_SCOPES, so this key was filtered out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing load is on workspace configuration initialization's critical path, but accepting one additional boolean does not add a boundary call or additional pass.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace settings document size; the diff changes classification of one fixed setting and does not alter load cardinality or parsing complexity materially.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One workspace configuration load/reload is awaited per workspace initialization; cached and file-service initialization are already sequenced, with no concurrency added by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing configuration caching remains unchanged: cached workspaces read the same cache and later initialize from the file service; uncached workspaces use the same direct load. No cache key, miss handling, invalidation, or coalescing changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the scope enum, WORKSPACE_SCOPES, and WorkspaceConfiguration load path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact configuration-file size and backend latency vary, but there is no changed boundary count or scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the existing single configuration read now retains one boolean instead of filtering it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or update the new-session composer with the experimental layout enabled from Agents settings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget reads the in-memory setting through an observable, toggles one CSS class, and reparents the single repository-controls element before requesting its existing responsive layout. This synchronous constant-size DOM work is on the render/configuration-change path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed number of composer controls and one repository-controls node per widget; cost does not scale with repositories, sessions, history, or settings count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A synchronous autorun handles each relevant configuration or session-state change; there is no parallel work, queue, subprocess, IPC, network call, or fan-out introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration values are served from the existing in-memory configuration model. The observable subscribes to existing configuration events; no new cache or repeated external lookup is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from NewChatWidget's observable/autorun and NewChatInputWidget.placeRepositoryControls implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout cost varies, but the traced operation is a bounded reparent/layout already implemented for this feature and is only newly reachable when the intentionally enabled setting applies.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the scope change enables intended constant-size UI behavior without repeated collection work, boundary calls, or retained growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load the browser regression-test module that verifies configuration scope
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test module evaluation imports the chat contribution once, reads the already-registered configuration property once, and then runs the assertion. This is test-only and off the product runtime critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One test module and one schema lookup, independent of product data size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single module initialization under the test runner; no added burst or repeated per-test import execution within the module cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ES module loading is cached by the test runtime; the captured schema object is a single module-level reference and does not grow across test cases.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the added static import and module-level registry lookup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The contribution import has broad registration side effects, but it is one-time test setup and no evidence shows material suite slowdown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable product performance regression and no concrete material test-performance mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed both changed files and traced configuration loading, scope filtering, composer consumption, DOM placement, and test module initialization. The PR changes one setting from application to window scope; it adds no expensive boundary, hot-path fan-out, unbounded retention, or scaling work. No findings or regression-fix records were warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
